memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob and his descendants) who went to Egypt: Reuben the firstborn of Jacob... The sons of Leah... were thirty-three in all." — Gen 46:8-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here begins a long list of names, and most of them we will never hear of again. Hezron. Zohar. Puah. Jahleel. Ordinary people, recorded forever because they belonged to God's family.

Do not skim past this too quickly. This list is God's way of saying that no one in His household is anonymous. Egypt would remember Joseph. History would remember Pharaoh. But God wrote down the names of shepherds' children who never did a single notable thing.

Look at Leah, too. She is named here as the mother of a third of this family — the wife Jacob did not choose, the one described as unloved (Gen 29:31). God saw her, and her sons became the largest branch of Israel. From her son Judah would come the Messiah, and from her son Levi the priesthood. The overlooked wife is at the centre of God's plan.

That is how God works. He does not build His purposes out of the impressive and the celebrated. He uses the unnoticed.

If you feel like a name nobody would record, remember that Christ says His people's names are written in heaven, and that this is a greater cause for rejoicing than anything else we could achieve (Lk 10:20).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever feel overlooked? What does this list say to you?
2. Where has God used something ordinary in your life for something bigger?
3. What difference does it make that your name is known to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know my name and that nothing about me is anonymous to You. When I feel unnoticed, remind me that my name is written in heaven. Amen.
